Mushi
mū'shī
n. (younger son of Merari and head of the Mushite family of Levites, whose descendants served in the temple courses under David)
From Hebrew Mushi, of uncertain derivation, perhaps connected with a root meaning to withdraw or depart. He is never named apart from Mahli his brother.

Biblical Definition

Mushi is the second son of Merari and the head of the Mushites, one of the two Merarite families of Levites (Exo 6:19; Num 3:20). Like his brother's house, his descendants carried the frame of the tabernacle through the wilderness. Where the record grows interesting is in the Chronicler, who traces the family into the settled worship of the temple. “The sons of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jeremoth, three” (1Ch 23:23) — and the son named Mahli after his uncle shows a family keeping its own memory. When David organized the Levites into courses for the house that Solomon would build, the Mushites were numbered in: “The sons also of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after the house of their fathers” (1Ch 24:30). And centuries after that, when Josiah repaired the temple, the overseers of the workmen included “Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari”, and the record adds that the men did the work faithfully (2Ch 34:12). Wilderness, monarchy, reformation: the same house, doing the same kind of work, for the better part of a thousand years.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Mushi; in sacred history he is the younger son of Merari, and head of the Mushite family of Levites.

expand to see more

MUSHI, n. The second son of Merari, the son of Levi.

From him descended the family of the Mushites.

His sons were Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth, named in the courses appointed by David.

With the Mahlites they bore the boards and pillars of the tabernacle in the wilderness.

Merarites of this line were overseers of the workmen when Josiah repaired the house of the LORD.

Key Scripture

Exo 6:19 — "And the sons of Merari; Mahali and Mushi: these are the families of Levi according to their generations."

1Ch 6:19 — "The sons of Merari; Mahli, and Mushi. And these are the families of the Levites according to their fathers."

1Ch 23:23 — "The sons of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jeremoth, three."

2Ch 34:12 — "And the men did the work faithfully: and the overseers of them were Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari; and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to set it forward; and other of the Levites, all that could skill of instruments of musick."

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is generational faithfulness — a house serving God in the same office across centuries, and a father's duty to hand on what he received.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The Mushites are a Levitical family and no controversy attaches to them. What their record supplies is a picture the modern church badly needs: continuity. The same house appears carrying boards in the wilderness, standing in David's courses, and overseeing Josiah's repairs, and Chronicles is careful to say of that last generation that they did the work faithfully. Nothing in it is spectacular. It is a family that kept doing its assigned work while kingdoms rose and fell around it.

The principle to recover is the deliberate handing-on of the faith from one generation to the next, which Scripture treats as a command rather than a hope. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house” (Deu 6:7); “the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also” (2Ti 2:2). A culture that treats each generation as free to reinvent its convictions produces exactly what Judges describes — a generation which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel (Jdg 2:10). The Mushites are the alternative, and their monument is a single line in Chronicles about doing the work faithfully.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mushi (H4187), Mushi; Merari (H4847), Merari; machaloqeth (H4256), division, course; 'emunah (H530), faithfulness; 'abodah (H5656), service, work.

expand to see more

Hebrew Mushi (H4187) — Mushi; younger son of Merari, head of the Mushites.

Hebrew Merari (H4847) — Merari; his father, the third son of Levi.

Hebrew machaloqeth (H4256) — division, course; the rota David appointed for the Levites.

Hebrew 'emunah (H530) — faithfulness, steadiness; “the men did the work faithfully”.

Hebrew 'abodah (H5656) — labour, service, ministry; the Levite's word for his work.

Usage

"“The sons of Merari; Mahli, and Mushi” — two brothers, two families, one charge."

"“The sons of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jeremoth, three” — a nephew named for his uncle."

"“The men did the work faithfully” — the epitaph the house earned."
